lastText: File ClosedWhat the Steppe KeptContestedSoviet High Command, 1941 — 1945End of hostilities: MARCH 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around March 1945 — earlier than the historical May 1945, bought with a faster, costlier advance. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over — a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. Operation Mars was scaled back rather than launched at full strength — sparing the Rzhev grinder's historical cost, a battle Soviet archives themselves stayed quiet about for fifty years. Stalin's train left Moscow in the October panic — the single most effective symbolic act of the historical Soviet war, not performed on this path, with a deeper and longer panic as the price. Order No. 227 was transmitted but its blocking detachments and penal machinery left to commanders' discretion — the argument some front commanders quietly practiced, made policy here. Germany's defeat was not a variable Soviet command decisions controlled, only its timing and its price.One Year LaterVictory arrived ahead of the historical May 1945, which means the occupation of eastern and central Europe has had that much longer to harden by the time this account picks back up a year later. Within the year, the governments this front's advance put in place across Eastern Europe are consolidating along lines this campaign's own choices shaped on
